why_ai: Accredited labs must physically test samples and products, and regulators and buyers mandate their certificates; AI cannot run the chemistry or the chamber.
why_clarity: Standard methods with QC limits give exact, checkable results on thousands of near-identical samples.
why_digital: Physical samples and products are tested at benches and in chambers; results go out as digital certificates to clients who still prefer nearby labs for sample logistics.

why_ai: Soil and water must be analysed on accredited instruments within holding times, but price-per-sample competition and automation erode the human share.
why_clarity: EPA methods with fixed QC acceptance limits give objective pass or fail on very high volumes.
why_digital: Physical samples analysed at benches; results delivered as electronic data deliverables to regional and national clients.

why_ai: Products must be physically tested and certified by recognised labs before market access, and certifiers carry accountability for the mark.
why_clarity: Standards define tests and limits exactly, though scoping and failure diagnosis vary by product.
why_digital: Physical products tested in labs and chambers; reports and certificates go digitally to manufacturers worldwide.

why_ai: Recognised certifiers test products and visit factories in person, and the mark's acceptance by inspectors and retailers is the product.
why_clarity: Listings specify construction and critical components exactly, and follow-up checks are pass or fail.
why_digital: Products and factories are physical; listings and variation notices are records sold to global manufacturers.

why_ai: Products must be measured in chambers by FCC-recognised labs, and failure diagnosis rests on senior engineers' judgement.
why_clarity: Emissions and radio limits are exact and a scan shows pass or fail at once, though debugging is done by feel.
why_digital: Hardware is tested in shielded chambers; reports are digital and clients ship products to labs in other countries.

why_ai: Certified technicians must sample concrete and soil on site and the code requires independent special inspection.
why_clarity: ASTM field and lab tests give exact pass or fail against the specification.
why_digital: Physical materials tested on site and in local labs, with paper-heavy reports issued to local projects.

why_ai: Someone must unpack coolers and check bottles by hand, but reading forms and checking rules is readily automated.
why_clarity: Login rules, holding times and preservation checks are written down and repeat on every cooler.
why_digital: Physical coolers and paper forms come in; the output is a LIMS record inside the lab.

why_ai: Small labs do the same physical accredited testing and keep clients through local relationships, though consolidation pressures them.
why_clarity: They run standard accredited methods with objective results, across a narrower but repetitive scope.
why_digital: Physical samples tested on local benches for nearby clients; reports delivered digitally.

why_ai: The quality manager is accountable for the management system and hosts assessors, but most record-keeping is automatable.
why_clarity: ISO/IEC 17025 clauses define what must exist, but assessment feedback arrives only every year or two.
why_digital: Works from documents, data and records on screen, with in-person assessments.

why_ai: Swabs and food samples must be enriched and tested physically by accredited labs; food safety demand is unaffected by AI.
why_clarity: Fixed protocols give positive or negative results on thousands of identical swabs.
why_digital: Physical swabs shipped to labs by courier; results delivered through portals to plants in the region.

why_ai: A signatory must release results and reviewer judgement is tacit, but most of the review is screen work that models can triage.
why_clarity: Acceptance criteria are written, but reading chromatography is done by feel and errors surface late.
why_digital: Raw data in, reviewed results and certificates out, all on screens inside the lab.

why_ai: Accreditation mandates participation and providers must make physical test materials, though scoring itself is statistical routine.
why_clarity: Assigned values and z-scores are computed by documented statistics on identical rounds.
why_digital: Physical samples go out and digital results come back from labs worldwide.

why_ai: Validation applies written EPA and DoD rules that software can apply, with a chemist's signature.
why_clarity: Qualifier rules, holding times and QC criteria are checked against written guidelines on every package.
why_digital: Lab data packages in, qualified datasets and validation reports out, entirely on screens.

why_ai: Reading public product law is increasingly model work; the maintained interpretation and the trust clients place in it are what protect the vendor.
why_clarity: Each regulation is classified and mapped in a repeatable way at volume, though applicability calls on ambiguous scope definitions vary.
why_digital: Public legal text in, classified content and alerts out, sold globally by subscription.

why_ai: Experts examine failed hardware and sign opinions they defend personally under cross-examination; demand rises with litigation, unaffected by AI.
why_clarity: Methods for failure analysis are documented, but each investigation differs and the answer is tested in court rather than checked quickly.
why_digital: Failed physical items and sites in, reports and testimony out, sold nationally through lawyers and insurers.

why_ai: Readers pay for a trusted independent brand that tests products physically, though AI review aggregators compete for attention.
why_clarity: Standardised protocols rate products consistently across categories.
why_digital: Products are bought and tested in labs; ratings are published online to a national audience.

why_ai: Building officials rely on the evaluation service's report and its acceptance by code bodies.
why_clarity: Acceptance criteria define what test evidence a product needs, and reports follow a fixed shape.
why_digital: Test reports in, evaluation reports out, sold to manufacturers nationwide.

why_ai: Programmes arrange physical verification testing and are relied on by regulators and utilities.
why_clarity: Rated performance is checked against measured performance with objective tolerances.
why_digital: Products tested at independent labs; directories are published online for national use.

why_ai: Assessors visit labs in person and accreditation decisions carry regulatory recognition.
why_clarity: ISO/IEC 17025 defines the criteria, but whether an accreditation decision was right shows only slowly.
why_digital: On-site assessment plus records review; certificates and reports delivered digitally.

why_ai: Bodies hold delegated authority to grant authorisations, though the review of test reports is routine.
why_clarity: FCC rules and test reports are checked against fixed requirements on every application.
why_digital: Test reports in, authorisation grants out, all online for global manufacturers.

why_ai: Auditors examine special processes on supplier floors in person, and primes require the accreditation decision of an accountable body.
why_clarity: Audit criteria are codified and recur across thousands of sites, though nonconformance judgements vary and outcomes show slowly.
why_digital: Physical supplier sites audited on site by travelling auditors; findings and decisions managed in an online system.

why_ai: Large-scale fire and hazard tests are physical and the insurer's approval is what policyholders must buy.
why_clarity: Approval standards define tests, though test programmes vary by product type.
why_digital: Products are burned and tested in large physical facilities; approval guides are published online.

why_ai: Certified materials must be made and characterised physically, and labs will keep buying them.
why_clarity: Characterisation follows documented metrology and certified values are checkable.
why_digital: A physical product made in a lab and shipped from a catalogue to buyers worldwide.

why_ai: Standards carry authority from consensus and from codes that cite them, which software cannot confer, though drafting and editing are automatable.
why_clarity: Standards follow a documented development procedure and recur on revision cycles, but whether a provision was right shows only over years.
why_digital: Drafted and balloted largely online, partly in committee meetings, and sold as documents worldwide.

why_ai: Internal benchmarking and deal models are screen work that analytics tools increasingly do.
why_clarity: Site benchmarks follow common metrics, but deal outcomes are known only years later.
why_digital: Operating and financial data in, internal models out, entirely on screens.

why_ai: Reviewers carry accountability for what is listed, but document review is increasingly automated.
why_clarity: Required certificates and test reports are checked against written protocols.
why_digital: Reports and certificates reviewed online for global suppliers and sellers.

why_ai: Federal authority to recognise labs cannot be delegated to software.
why_clarity: Recognition criteria are written, but whether a recognised lab performs well shows slowly.
why_digital: Applications and data reviewed on screen, with some on-site audits, under federal jurisdiction.

why_ai: Software products face AI-native competitors and code generation directly.
why_clarity: Configurations repeat by lab type and releases are tested objectively.
why_digital: Software built and delivered online to labs worldwide.

why_ai: Associations rest on member relationships and convening, which AI does not replace.
why_clarity: Advocacy and consensus work has no checkable deliverable.
why_digital: Meetings, surveys and documents, partly in person and partly online.

why_ai: Labs hire a trusted former assessor, though templates and AI tools cover much of the paperwork.
why_clarity: ISO/IEC 17025 defines what must be produced, but success shows only at the assessment.
why_digital: Documents produced remotely with occasional site visits, for labs found through referrals.
